why: offset everywhere incl. toc and CLI, validated, documented and tested
prompt:
Add a `heading_offset` option to `markdown.Markdown` (and `markdown.markdown`): a whole number from 0 to 5, default 0, that shifts the level of every heading Markdown produces by that many (an `h1` becomes an `h2` with 1), never beyond `h6`. Any other value raises `ValueError`.
- It applies to hash and underline headings, and to headings from extensions such as `md_in_html`.
- The `toc` extension sees the shifted levels (its tokens and `toc_depth`).
- The command line gets `--heading-offset N`.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer:
Added `heading_offset` (0–5, default 0, anything else raises `ValueError`) to `markdown.Markdown`/`markdown.markdown` and `--heading-offset N` to the command line; the full test suite passes (1154 tests, 112 skipped), with no linter available here to check style.

It is implemented as a built-in tree processor (`heading_offset`, priority 25) that shifts every `h1`–`h6` element in the parsed tree, capped at `h6`. That covers hash and underline headings, `md_in_html` headings, and headings inside footnotes, and `toc` sees the shifted levels in its tokens and `toc_depth`.

Behaviours you might not expect:
- **Raw HTML headings are not shifted.** A plain `<h1>` in the source passes through unchanged. A raw heading nested inside an `md_in_html` `markdown="1"` block is shifted, because that extension puts it in the tree.
- **`toc` `baselevel` stacks on top of the offset**, still capped at `h6`.
- **`True`/`False`, `1.0` and `'1'` are rejected** with `ValueError`, not just out-of-range integers.
- **CLI out-of-range values** (e.g. `--heading-offset 7`) exit with a usage error, code 2, rather than a traceback.
- **`parse_options` only includes `heading_offset` when the flag is given**, so the existing CLI option tests, which compare the whole options dict, still pass unchanged.

Docs are updated (`library.md`, `cli.md`, `extensions/toc.md`, `extensions/api.md`) with an Unreleased changelog entry. The `cli.md` help listing also gained the `-n, --no_lazy_ol` line, which was missing from the documented output.
